exact_text: PLAN §8.4: ‘Control degradation always commits durably and atomically fences active exposure before any later receipt.’
IR36 reaches WIDENING_REVIEW while ‘old bounds remain’; IR41 later identifies degradation/staleness there and explicitly says ‘stop exposure’.

Generic IH01 is legal at WIDENING_REVIEW because that rollout is outside the six-state active set, but IH01 only records degradation and stops admission; it does not fence or stop the still-existing exposure.

findings.title: Control degradation at WIDENING_REVIEW does not atomically fence the active widening exposure
findings.requirement: PLAN §8.4 requires every control degradation to commit durably and atomically fence active exposure, and manifest §15.7 claims coverage of every canary/exposure interval.
evidence: IR36 moves CANARY_RUNNING to WIDENING_REVIEW and states that old bounds remain; unlike the paused path, it does not say those bounds are stopped.
IR41 confirms WIDENING_REVIEW can receive a telemetry/stale-manifest degradation and explicitly performs ‘stop exposure’. This makes an exposure-bearing WIDENING_REVIEW tuple reachable.
The §15.7 active set is only CANARY_RUNNING, WIDENING_EFFECT, APPROVED, PROMOTING, PROMOTED, and OBSERVING. Therefore WIDENING_REVIEW selects generic IH01.
IH01 records degradation and stops admission only. It does not revoke/fence authority or stop the existing exposure, unlike IH01-C/W/A/P/WV/PV/D/O and IR41.
findings.impact: A degradation can commit in a reachable exposure-bearing widening-review tuple while the exposure remains live. Later ordinary progress rejects because health is stale, but the required atomic stop/fence never occurred. This contradicts PLAN §8.4 and leaves an unsafe control-loss interval.
findings.required_correction: Add a synchronized HEALTHY-to-TELEMETRY_DEGRADED interrupt for exposure-bearing WIDENING_REVIEW (and any other generated exposure-bearing review coordinate), atomically fence authority/sends and stop exposure, then include it in the sole-interrupt equality and witnesses. Alternatively, prove and encode that WIDENING_REVIEW never retains live exposure; that would require changing IR36/IR39/IR40 and the generated reachable relation.

findings.title: A first cancellation request after BUILD/MAINTENANCE reaches ROLLED_BACK has no legal private edge
findings.requirement: The owner cancellation contract and closed manifests require authenticated cancel to have a defined path from every reachable nonterminal factory state, with exact replay and one cleanup owner.
evidence: B38 and M29 reach ROLLED_BACK after rollback settlement and block release. ROLLED_BACK remains nonterminal until B39/M30 or the cancellation continuation.
B66-B70 and M54-M58 can persist cancellation only while rollback is REQUESTED, ROLLING_BACK, ROLLBACK_VERIFYING, ROLLBACK_FAILED, or ROLLBACK_VERIFIED; B75/M63 cover REMEDIATION_WAIT.
B71/M59 require the cancellation disposition already to be persisted. The surrounding prose expressly partitions B39/M30 on absence versus B71/M59 on presence of that persisted disposition.
There is no ROLLED_BACK self/adoption row that persists a newly arriving authenticated cancellation, and canonical CW-C64 is likewise described as cancellation ‘persisted during rollback’.
findings.impact: If cancel arrives after B38/M29 commits but before ordinary cleanup begins, B39/M30 is no longer the requested disposition while B71/M59 cannot satisfy their persisted-disposition guard. A literal closed-edge implementation must reject or strand a valid cancel, or invent unlisted persistence semantics. This is an undefined reachable cancellation race.
findings.required_correction: Either add exact ROLLED_BACK first-arrival cancellation rows that atomically authenticate, persist the disposition, advance the epoch/revoke, and enter CANCEL_REQUESTED, or redefine B71/M59 unambiguously as that atomic absent-to-persisted transaction and separately specify replay of cancellation persisted during rollback. Preserve mutual exclusion with B39/M30 by one expected-version/disposition CAS and add witnesses for cancel both before and after B38/M29.
